The Specialty Outpatient Staff Registered Nurse (RN) is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based specialty care to patients with oversight of licensed vocational nurses/nursing assistants as appropriate to clinic setting.

Duties include but are not limited to: Patient care, care coordination, health promotion, health education and coaching on wellness, disease prevention, and chronic care management Assists in directing the provision of nursing education, orientation, competencies and providing quality improvement and outcomes utilization Demonstrates leadership in delivering and improving holistic, specialty care through collaborative strategies with others.

Evaluates practice in an ongoing process, based on best evidence.

Provides peers with informal constructive feedback for improvement Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of healthcare professionals Contributes professional nursing perspect in discussions with the interdisciplinary team Leads the integration of evidence-based practice/research with clinical expertise to improve quality of care and resource utilization with improved outcomes for the immediate practice setting Expands knowledge base and practice evaluation through mentoring, precepting, and/or teaching VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory Work Schedule: Full-Time, Monday-Friday, Day shift Compressed/Flexible: This position is not eligible.

Telework: This position is not eligible. Virtual: This is not a virtual position. Financial Disclosure Report: Not required. Notifications: This position is an AFGE Bargaining Unit position. Selectee may be required to work at any VA Connecticut Healthcare System campus, as needed.

Current and former Federal employees must submit copies of their most recent SF-50 (Notice of Personnel Action). The SF-50 must identify the position title, series, grade, step, tenure and type of service (Competitive or Excepted). In some cases, more than one SF-50 may be required to show a higher grade previously held.

This position is in the Excepted Service. The salary is based on the grade and step approved for the selected candidate.
Basic Requirements: English Language Proficiency. In accordance with 38 U.S.C. 7403(f), no person shall serve in direct patient care positions unless they are proficient in basic written and spoken English.

Graduate of a school of professional nursing approved by the appropriate accrediting agency and accredited by one of the following accrediting bodies at the time the program was completed by the applicant: The Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN) or The Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE); OR Individuals attending a master's level bridge program in nursing who have completed coursework equivalent to a bachelor's level degree in Nursing may have opportunity to become registered as a nurse with a state licensing board prior to completion of the bridge program.

Upon achievement of a State license, the individual may be appointed on temporary basis and later converted to a permanent appointment upon successful completion and graduation from the bridge program.

(Reference VA Handbook 5005, Appendix G6); OR In cases of graduates of foreign schools of professional nursing, possession of a current, full, active, and unrestricted registration will meet the requirement for graduation from an approved school of professional nursing to warrant an appointment as a Nurse who has completed an associated degree/entry level Nursing education program.

Credit for foreign nursing education higher that associate degree/entry level requires a formal degree equivalency validation from a recognized equivalency evaluation accepted by VA such as International Consultants of Delaware (ICD).

Current, full, active, and unrestricted registration as a graduate professional nurse in a State, Territory or Commonwealth (i.e., Puerto Rico) of the United States, or the District of Columbia.

Graduate Nurse Technician (GNT) Exception: Candidates who otherwise meet the basic education requirements, but do not possess the required licensure, may be appointed at the entry step of the grade and level applicable to the completed nursing education as a GNT on a 120-day temporary appointment while actively pursuing licensure (may be extended up to two years on a case-by-case-basis.) Nurse I, Level II Demonstrates integration of biopsychosocial concepts, cognitive skills and technically competent practice in providing care to clients with basic or complex.

An ADN or Diploma in Nursing AND 1 year of specialized nursing experience equivalent to Nurse I, Level 1 ;OR a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) with no additional professional nursing experience required. Nurse I, Level III Demonstrates proficiency in practice based on conscious and deliberate planning.

Self-directed in goal setting for managing complex client situations.

An ADN or Diploma in Nursing AND 2 years of professional nursing experience in which one year is equivalent to Nurse I, Level 2; OR a BSN and 1 year of professional nursing experience equivalent to the Nurse I, Level 2; OR a Master's degree in nursing (MSN) and no additional professional nursing experience; OR a Master's degree in a *related field with a BSN and no additional professional nursing experience.

Duties include but not limited to: Designs/redesigns, implements, evaluates, and maintains the medical center's risk management program and supports the patient safety, risk management program. Demonstrates expertise in the interpretation and application of standards, directives, and regulations related to the risk management program.

Ensures the healthcare system is in compliance with regulatory and accreditation standards and directives related to quality and risk management functions. Participates in the adverse event reporting process including analysis and follow up as needed.

Acts as a consultant to the clinical staff on disclosure of the adverse event process and participates in the disclosure process when requested by leadership. Supports other investigative reviews such as Fact Finding and AIBs. Focus is on individual growth and development in practice with increased levels of self-direction.

Brings principles and theory with limited application of critical thinking skills. Has a global understanding of how their area(s) of responsibility supports the system's mission and vision.

Responsible and accountable for the planning, organization, and evaluation of effectiveness related to critical, informatics, and/or administrative process changes, analyzing issues impeding change, developing corrective actions to expedite change, and assuring optimum utilization of available resources to maintain a climate conducive to quality patient care and employee satisfaction.

Functions as formal and informal educator; serving as a liaison between internal and external customers, supporting factors that impact customer satisfaction, considering the client population, including age and life stages, state of health, race and culture, values, and previous experiences.

Influence care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team. This position potentially requires flexibility in schedule and assignments. This may include but is not limited to medication administration and ADLs. Travel may be required up to 25%.

This role combines clinical proficiency with leadership responsibilities and is often considered part of the succession plan for future NM positions, providing opportunities to develop management skills and prepare for higher-level leadership.

Functions as a proficient clinician and is responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing or overseeing direct patient care. Assesses, plans, implements, and evaluates delivery of care based on age specific components.

Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care. Demonstrates sound decision-making and judgment and possess excellent interpersonal skills.

Self-directed and influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team and leading innovative process improvement initiatives. While working in partnership with the Nurse Manager, functions as a Supervisor and Clinical Coordinator assuming responsibility for the operation of the designated unit.

This may include: onsite coverage at designated CBOC(s) per the assigned Northern Tier/Southern Tier, participating in the hiring process; supervising and ongoing evaluation of care delivered by all nursing staff and employees assigned to the CBOC/Annex via Nursing Proficiencies and icr performance appraisals.

The ANM is charged with contributing to the establishment and implementation of evidence based nursing standard of practice, monitoring the quality of care by means such as 2-day post discharge, including any other primary care related reports, scores, reminders or PACT quality indicators.

ANM will also assure all education, competencies and staff orientations process in the unit are complete with consultation with NM.

ANM will assist the P1 process and keep track of the progress of P1 projects, All Employee Survey Results, Press Ganey responses, SHEP scores, VSignals, Hand Hygiene, and MDRO Teaching to ensure quality care to our Veteran Patients.

The ANM is accountable to address storage, recall and replacement of medications, including transportation of specimen and medications. Assist with addressing and maintaining building operations in collaboration with Nurse Manager and Clinic Manager as well as the property owner, VA environmental services, and VA engineering services.

The ANM will provide oversight of staffing needs, leave request, and payroll. The ANM will provide hands-on clinical support in the nurse PACT roles during times of limited staffing resources. The ANM will facilitate HRO huddles as needed.

The ANM will facilitate and or assist with nurse staff meetings. he ANM has the authority to provide verbal and written counseling in collaboration with HR, Union and NM. ANM will need to promote and adhere to the PACT model of care.

The ANM will promote, create, demonstrate and ensure a positive, culturally diverse work force in which the values and needs of all individual are respected while enhancing patient care delivery and professional development of Nursing staff. The ANM will manage the CBOC/Annex in the absence of the Nurse Manager.

Major Duties include, but are not limited to: The Nurse Manager is the designated first-line supervisory authority and is responsible and accountable for the operation of their assigned units and provides coverage for other NMs as needed.

Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care. Responsible and accountable for the direction and supervision of specific orientation, training, development of staff, and evaluation of individual staff performance.

Functions as a role model, educator, practitioner, and supervisor providing leadership to the team. Enhances care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team to remove barriers and implement new evidence-based cutting-edge programs/processes.

Equips staff with tools for competent care and promotes an environment of accountability for high-quality, cost-effective outcomes. Contributes to the development of care delivery models and environmental design, ensuring evidence-based, accessible, affordable patient care.

Aligns nursing/clinical objectives with organizational strategic outcomes, participating in strategy planning and execution. Maintains knowledge and ensures compliance with all regulatory and accreditation standards, Directives, policies, and standard operating procedures (SOP).

Contributes professional nursing perspective in discussions with the interdisciplinary team. This position potentially requires flexibility in schedule and assignments. All other duties as assigned.

Preferred Experience: Progressive Leadership, Care Coordination Physical Requirements: This position includes a level of physicality normally associated with duties performed by nurses such as direct patient care, and potentially long periods of walking, standing, sitting, moderate lifting, repeated bending, or kneeling.

Examples may include but are not limited to: - Significant amounts of time standing assisting patients - Utilization of safe patient handling and mobility protocols.

Major Duties: Clinical Operations & Patient Safety - Ensures continuous monitoring and safety checks in accordance with suicidal and homicidal risk protocols, contraband prevention procedures, elopement policies, and mental health observation standards. - Oversees implementation of trauma-informed care, de-escalation strategies, and approved behavioral management interventions (e.g., CPI/PMDB-trained approaches). - Ensures staff competency in psychiatric emergency response, including Code Green/behavioral rapid response procedures, and safe application of seclusion/restraint in strict accordance with regulatory standards. - Monitors trends in behavioral incidents and leads corrective action plans to improve unit safety.

Staff Supervision & Development - Directs psychiatric nursing staff in performing mental status assessments, behavior documentation, therapeutic communication, medication administration, and withdrawal monitoring. - Ensures staff maintain competency in suicide prevention, recovery model principles, substance use disorder protocols, and management of acute psychiatric symptoms. - Provides real-time coaching during high-acuity events (e.g., escalation, aggressive behaviors, rapid clinical deterioration).

Interdisciplinary Collaboration - Actively participates in and coordinates daily treatment team rounds, reviewing each Veteran's psychiatric symptoms, progress, barriers to discharge, and recovery goals. - Partners closely with psychiatry providers on medication changes, behavioral plans, and crisis interventions. - Engages social work on discharge planning, safety planning, and coordination with outpatient MH programs such as PRRC, HUD-VASH, and SUD services.

Quality & Compliance - Ensures adherence to Joint Commission Behavioral Health standards, VA mental health policies, seclusion/restraint regulations, and documentation requirements for high-risk patients. - Leads performance improvement projects specific to inpatient psychiatry such as falls in MH populations, seclusion/restraint reduction, suicide risk management, and aggression mitigation. - Facilitates Root Cause Analyses and safety huddles related to psychiatric care events.

Environment of Care - Maintains a ligature-resistant environment; ensures staff reporting, maintenance follow-up, and environmental rounds are completed timely. - Collaborates with engineering and MH leadership on safety enhancements and compliance with ligature-risk mitigation plans.

Veteran-Centered Mental Health Care - Ensures individualized therapeutic interventions, including psychoeducation, coping skills development, crisis stabilization, and recovery planning. - Promotes Veteran engagement in group therapies, treatment planning, and self-management activities. - Monitors patient experience feedback specific to mental health care (e.g., perceptions of safety, therapeutic engagement, staff responsiveness).

## L'entreprise : HUG ##
Avec plus de 13'000 collaborateurs et collaboratrices représentant 160 métiers, les Hôpitaux Universitaires de Genève sont un établissement de référence au niveau national et international. Pour en savoir plus sur notre institution, prenez quelques minutes pour consulter notre rétrospective 2025 en cliquant ici.
Le Département de médecine de premier recours (DMPR) a pour mission sociétale de permettre un accès aux soins de qualité pour tous par une médecine de proximité, d'assurer la prise en charge des urgences médicales et chirurgicales légères, de promouvoir la prévention auprès des citoyennes et citoyens, d'apporter les connaissances médicales aux investigations judiciaires et de promouvoir la santé des voyageurs et voyageuses.
Le service de médecine tropicale et humanitaire assure la prise en charge de patients ayant voyagé et présentant une pathologie d'importation, tropicale ou parasitaire et prodigue des conseils de prévention. Il effectue des vaccinations spécialisées pour les voyageurs, les expatriés, les étudiants et la population locale. Par ailleurs, ce service participe activement aux interventions vaccinales en cas d'épidémie ou autre besoin identifié.

## Description du poste ##
En qualité d'infirmier ou infirmière au Service de médecine tropicale et humanitaire (SMTH), votre mission consiste à mener de manière autonome des consultations infirmières de pré-voyage auprès d'une patientèle très diversifiée (expatriés, familles, humanitaires, immunosupprimés).
Vous menez et gérez des consultations infirmières de première ligne de manière autonome, dans le respect des missions, des protocoles et des délégations qui vous sont confiés.
Vous assurez également une activité de conseil aux voyageurs et voyageuses en formulant des recommandations personnalisées en matière de prévention des risques liés au voyage (vaccinations, prophylaxie, mesures d'hygiène, prévention des maladies infectieuses et autres risques sanitaires). Vous participez activement aux campagnes de vaccinations sur différents sites.
Vous travaillez en collaboration avec une équipe pluriprofessionnelle ainsi qu'avec les réseaux de soins internes et externes, notamment les organisations non gouvernementales, les organisations internationales et les partenaires présents au Global Health Campus.
Votre empathie, votre sens du relationnel et votre capacité à créer un climat de confiance vous permettent de vous positionner comme un partenaire de soins à part entière.
Doté ou dotée d'une excellente capacité d'adaptation et de l'organisation, vous êtes en mesure de faire face à des flux de patients importants et variables tout en maintenant une prise en charge de qualité. Vous gérez sereinement les imprévus et les situations génératrices de stress.
Vous possédez d'excellentes compétences relationnelles, un sens développé d l'accueil et une communication bienveillante, vous permettant de répondre aux attentes d'une patientèle exigeante et multiculturelle.
Dans le cadre de votre activité, vous êtes amené ou amenée à intervenir sur deux sites.
## Description du profil ##
Vous possédez un Bachelor HES en soins infirmiers ou un diplôme en soins infirmiers équivalent reconnu par la Croix-Rouge suisse.
Vous avez une pratique professionnelle diversifiée de plus de 4 ans dans le domaine de la santé publique et/ou en santé communautaire et des connaissances en vaccinologie. Vous êtes au bénéfice d'une formation à l'évaluation clinique infirmière.
Une formation en médecine tropicale et des voyageurs constitue un réel atout.
Vous disposez d'un très bon niveau d'anglais, tant à l'oral qu'à l'écrit. La maitrise d'une autre langue, constitue un atout.
Vous savez vous adapter à divers contextes, aux imprévus, aux variations de charge de travail.
Vous possédez d'excellentes compétences relationnelles, un sens de l'accueil d'une communication bienveillante.

Collaborates and communicates with physicians and other staff to interpret, adjust, and coordinate patient care plan to ensure continuity of care. Accurately records all physician orders and treatment information in the individual patient medical record.

Responsable des soins
=====================
Maisonneuve est engagé dans la réadaptation aux côtés des personnes fragilisées par un accident, une maladie ou les effets du temps, en offrant à chacun un accompagnement personnalisé, respectueux et exigeant, à chaque étape de son parcours de soins.
Pour couvrir cette mission, Maisonneuve a mis en place un « écosystème » permettant de prendre en charge le patient en réadaptation stationnaire, ambulatoire et de l’accompagner à domicile.

s.h: Nous opérons à travers trois structures principales
s.t:
* La Clinique Châtelaine pour des patients en suite de soins aigus, spécialisée dans la réadaptation musculosquelettique, la médecine interne, l’oncologie et la gériatrie.
* CARE Charmilles, un centre ambulatoire de réadaptation.
* Maisonneuve à Domicile, destiné aux patients de la Clinique Châtelaine, pour assurer les soins à leur sortie.
En 2026, deux nouvelles structures ont ouvert leurs portes à Belle\-Terre, Thônex, composées d’une clinique stationnaire, Clinique Belle\-Terre, et d'un centre ambulatoire de réadaptation, CARE Belle\-Terre.
Dans le cadre de la croissance de notre structure, nous sommes à la recherche, pour la Clinique Chatelaine, d’un\-e :
**Responsable des soins**
-------------------------
Votre mission
-------------
En tant que Responsable des soins, vous assurez le pilotage, l'organisation et la coordination des activités de soins afin de garantir des prises en charge de qualité, sécurisées et centrées sur le patient. Vous veillez à la continuité des parcours de soins, accompagnez les équipes soignantes et contribuez activement au développement d'une culture d'excellence, de qualité et de sécurité au sein de l'établissement.
### Pilotage et coordination des soins
Vous coordonnez les parcours de soins, de l'admission à la sortie du patient, en veillant à leur fluidité, leur continuité et leur efficience. Vous favorisez une collaboration étroite entre les équipes soignantes, le corps médical, les thérapeutes et les partenaires du réseau afin de garantir une prise en charge interdisciplinaire de qualité et une expérience patient optimale.
### Organisation et qualité des soins
Vous organisez les activités du service afin d'assurer une prise en charge efficiente, conforme aux bonnes pratiques et aux exigences réglementaires. Vous garantissez l'application des procédures et protocoles, assurez le suivi des indicateurs qualité et sécurité, participez aux démarches d'amélioration continue et collaborez étroitement avec la Direction Qualité pour le déploiement des projets institutionnels.
### Management des équipes
Vous encadrez, accompagnez et développez les équipes soignantes en favorisant un environnement de travail collaboratif, bienveillant et responsabilisant. Vous assurez la planification des ressources, accompagnez le changement, soutenez le développement des compétences et veillez à maintenir une dynamique d'équipe favorisant la qualité des soins.
### Formation et développement
Vous supervisez l'accueil, l'intégration et l'encadrement des nouveaux collaborateurs, étudiants et stagiaires. Vous identifiez les besoins de formation, encouragez le développement des compétences et contribuez à la diffusion des bonnes pratiques professionnelles au sein des équipes.

--------------
* Bachelor HES en soins infirmiers ou diplôme reconnu en Suisse.
* Formation en management ou volonté de la suivre.
* Expérience confirmée en management d'équipe, idéalement en milieu hospitalier ou en réadaptation.
* Excellente connaissance des parcours de soins, des démarches qualité et des exigences réglementaires suisses.
* Leadership, sens de l'organisation, esprit d'équipe et capacité à accompagner le changement.

---------------------------------
* Un environnement de travail humain et collaboratif, centré sur le patient.

* Des opportunités de formation continue et de développement professionnel.
* Une collaboration interdisciplinaire favorisant l'innovation et l'amélioration continue des pratiques.
